exposure: distance of defect from internal os
outcome: histopathological changes at scar defect site
cohort: 44 non-pregnant women with abnormal gynecological symptoms and a history of at least 1 cesarean delivery with a cesarean section scar defect (niche) visualized on transvaginal ultrasound.
finding: Larger cesarean scar defects are associated with increased clinical symptoms (especially postmenstrual bleeding) and histopathological changes (congested endometrial fold, distortion of lower uterine segment, and disorganized muscle fibers).
followup_time: Time elapsed between last cesarean delivery and first consultation (exact timeframe not specified)
